events.reason: Abdominal pain and change in bowel habits

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: change in bowel habit with weight loss, father with colon cancer

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: belly cramps, bowels off.

HPI: 55F. About 2 months of crampy lower abdominal pain that lets up after she has a BM. Swings between a few days of constipation and then loose stools. Lately the cramps have been waking her at night, which is new. Not hungry - a lot of pressure at work this quarter, she's skipping lunch. Scale at home is down several pounds and it's confirmed here. No travel, no antibiotics, no blood she has noticed, no vomiting.

Meds unchanged: levothyroxine, MTX 15/wk, folic acid, pred 5, clobetasol twice weekly.

Exam: vitals and weight noted, down from 68 kg. Abdomen soft, mildly tender in both lower quadrants without guarding, no masses, bowel sounds normal.

A/P
Altered bowel habit with nocturnal symptoms and weight loss in a 55yo whose father had colon cancer; last colonoscopy 2016. Not something to watch. Urgent GI referral for evaluation and colonoscopy; they'll do the workup labs. If pain becomes severe, fever, or bleeding, call same day.
RA/thyroid stable.

events.reason: Abdominal pain, altered bowel habit, weight loss

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GI consultation, 04/14/2025.

55-year-old with hypothyroidism and RA on methotrexate and prednisone, also followed for restless legs and lichen sclerosus. Two months of lower abdominal cramping relieved by defecation, mixed constipation and diarrhea, now worse at night, and ten pounds of weight loss over the same period that she puts down to poor appetite under work stress. No travel or recent antibiotics. Father with colorectal cancer at 65. Last colonoscopy 2016, normal.

Exam: abdomen soft, mild diffuse tenderness, no rebound or guarding. Rectal exam unremarkable.

Labs: hemoglobin 10.8 g/dL, MCV 74 fL, ferritin 15 ng/mL, CRP 8 mg/L, tissue transglutaminase IgA negative.

Assessment: microcytic iron deficiency anemia with altered bowel habit and weight loss; celiac serology negative. A colonic source needs to be excluded.

Plan: colonoscopy, scheduled 05/08. Ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily. We will send the report.

Outpatient Gastroenterology

conditions.label: Benign neoplasm of ascending colon
conditions.note: 22 mm tubulovillous adenoma with high-grade dysplasia, resected by EMR

reports.text:
Specimen: ascending colon polyp, endoscopic mucosal resection, piecemeal, multiple fragments up to 1.4 cm in aggregate 2.3 cm.

Microscopic: adenomatous epithelium with tubular and villous architecture. Foci of high-grade dysplasia. No invasive carcinoma identified in the material examined.
reports.conclusion: Tubulovillous adenoma with high-grade dysplasia. Negative for invasive carcinoma.

documents.title: Colonoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Colonoscopy 05/08/2025. Indication: iron deficiency anemia, change in bowel habit, weight loss, family history of colorectal cancer.

Monitored anesthesia care. Prep good. Cecum reached and identified by appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve; terminal ileum not intubated. Withdrawal time 14 minutes.

Findings: a 22 mm sessile polyp in the ascending colon, lifted with submucosal injection and removed by endoscopic mucosal resection in several pieces; defect margins inspected with no visible residual tissue; defect closed with 3 clips. The remainder of the colon was normal to the cecum. Retroflexion in the rectum unremarkable.

Impression: large ascending colon polyp, resected. No other abnormality.

Recommendations: await pathology. Continue iron. Because the resection was piecemeal, repeat colonoscopy in about 6 months to check the site. Copy to PCP.

conditions.label: History of adenomatous colon polyps
conditions.note: advanced adenoma (tubulovillous, high-grade dysplasia), ascending colon

documents.title: Colonoscopy and pathology reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: GI report and pathology arrived today. 22 mm ascending colon polyp removed piecemeal, tubulovillous adenoma with high-grade dysplasia, no cancer. Called her - relieved. This is the likely bleeding source for her iron deficiency. Reviewed: keep taking iron daily, GI wants a look at the site in ~6 months. Suggested she let her sister know, since with their dad's history this is worth mentioning to her own doctor. Recheck CBC and ferritin in July.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Bowels have been much more regular since the colonoscopy, the night cramping stopped. Appetite back, weight coming up. Taking iron daily with a little constipation she manages with fiber. Legs at night a bit better too.

O: weight 66 kg (63.5 at GI in April). Abdomen soft, nontender.

A/P
Iron deficiency anemia from colon adenoma, improving. CBC and ferritin today. Continue iron.
Advanced adenoma s/p EMR - surveillance colonoscopy due around November per GI.
Physical next month.

documents.title: CBC and ferritin
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 11.6, up from 10.8. Ferritin 32, up from 15. Moving the right way. Continue iron, recheck at a later visit.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 55F.

Good stretch. Bowels normal, eating well, weight stable at 66. No fevers or sweats, no new lumps. Joints ok on her RA regimen. Skin controlled on twice-weekly clobetasol. RLS occasional.

Meds: levothyroxine 100 mcg, methotrexate 15 mg weekly, folic acid 1 mg, prednisone 5 mg, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, clobetasol 0.05% twice weekly.

Exam: well appearing. Neck supple, no lymphadenopathy, thyroid normal. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Breasts no masses. Abdomen soft, nontender. Hands without active synovitis. No edema.

A/P
1. HM - mammogram ordered. Pap/HPV done 2024. Colonoscopy surveillance per GI in the fall. Flu/COVID in October. PHQ-2 0.
2. Hypothyroidism - TSH.
3. Iron deficiency - CBC deferred, rechecked last month; continue iron.
4. RA, LS, RLS - stable, per specialists.
CMP, lipids, TSH today.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison 2021 through 2024. Heterogeneously dense breasts. No suspicious mass, calcification or architectural distortion. Unchanged.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Flu vaccine R deltoid, 2025-26 COVID L deltoid. Screening questions negative. Left after 15 min without problems.

events.reason: Night sweats, fevers, weight loss, neck mass

orders.order: General surgery referral for excisional lymph node biopsy
orders.reason: left cervical lymphadenopathy with B symptoms

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED visit 10/21/2025, brief summary.

55F with hypothyroidism, RA on methotrexate and prednisone, and a colon adenoma removed earlier this year. Two months of night sweats, low-grade fevers at home and about 10 lb of weight loss she was not trying for. Has felt a lump on the left side of her neck that has slowly grown. Home meds as listed by patient: levothyroxine, folic acid. NKDA.

Exam: firm, rubbery, non-tender 3 cm lymph node in the left cervical chain. No hepatosplenomegaly.

Labs: Hgb 11.2, WBC 7,000, platelets 250,000, LDH 245, ESR 50, ANA positive, RF elevated.

Impression: cervical lymphadenopathy with constitutional symptoms, concerning for lymphoma.

Disposition: stable for discharge. Urgent outpatient excisional node biopsy arranged with general surgery. Return for high fevers, trouble swallowing or breathing. PCP notified.

documents.title: Post-ED call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Read the ED note and called her. Frightened but organized. Surgery has her for excisional biopsy of the left neck node on 10/30. Explained what the biopsy tells us and that I'll call as soon as pathology is back. She asked about her methotrexate - told her not to change anything until we have a diagnosis and rheum weighs in. Reminded her she can call or text me directly with questions.

events.reason: Excisional biopsy, left cervical lymph node

conditions.label: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, lymph nodes of head, face, and neck

reports.text:
Specimen: lymph node, left neck, excisional biopsy. Received fresh, 3.2 x 2.4 x 1.9 cm.

Microscopic: nodal architecture is effaced by a diffuse proliferation of large lymphoid cells. Immunohistochemistry supports a B-cell lineage.

documents.title: Surgical pathology received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Lymph node pathology from general surgery (biopsy 10/30) received by fax. Flagged urgent to PCP.

documents.title: Lymph node pathology discussed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with her husband on speaker. Node shows diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Talked through what that means in plain terms: an aggressive but often curable lymphoma, treatment is usually chemo-immunotherapy, staging scan comes first. Urgent heme/onc referral placed, they can see her Monday 11/10. Called rheumatology to let them know given methotrexate; they will coordinate with oncology on stopping it. She knows to reach me any time.

medications.reason: stopped at lymphoma diagnosis with rheumatology agreement

documents.title: Hematology/Oncology Consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Hematology/Oncology new patient consultation, 11/10/2025.

Diagnosis: diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, left cervical lymph node, excised 10/30/2025.

55-year-old woman with seropositive RA treated with methotrexate and prednisone, hypothyroidism, and an advanced colon adenoma removed in May. Two months of night sweats, low-grade fevers and 10 lb weight loss with an enlarging left neck node.

Staging: PET-CT 11/07/2025 shows FDG-avid lymph nodes in the left neck only, the largest 3.1 cm. No other nodal or extranodal disease; bone marrow and spleen not involved. Stage I with B symptoms.

Pre-treatment: hepatitis B surface antigen and core antibody negative. HIV negative. Echocardiogram LVEF 60%.

Plan: methotrexate stopped today in agreement with her rheumatologist; folic acid stopped with it. R-CHOP every 21 days for 6 cycles, first cycle 11/13/2025. She continues prednisone 5 mg daily on the days she is not taking the chemotherapy prednisone. Restaging PET after completion. Supportive medicines will be prescribed by our clinic.

Thank you for referring her.
Hematology/Oncology

documents.title: Two down
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just checking in - second round of chemo was last Thursday. Tired for about a week after each one and some nausea the first few days, the oncology nurses gave me medicine for it and it mostly works. The lump in my neck already feels smaller. Joints feel better than they have in ages, oddly. I'm working from home on the bad days.

documents.title: RE: Two down
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: So good to hear the node is shrinking already. Lean on the oncology team for nausea or fevers - a fever during chemo is a call-them-right-away situation. Let's do a short video check-in in January.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, pt at home, identity verified.

Four cycles of R-CHOP done, last 1/15. Fatigue worst days 3-7 after each cycle, nausea controlled with the oncology regimen. No fevers since starting treatment, sweats gone. Eating ok. Neck node no longer palpable to her. Joints quiet. Still taking levothyroxine, prednisone 5 on non-chemo days, iron.

A/P
DLBCL on R-CHOP, tolerating. Per oncology.
Hypothyroidism - stable, TSH at next in-person visit.
RA quiet off methotrexate.
Check in after restaging in the spring.

documents.title: Done!
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Sixth and last treatment was February 26th. They rang the bell for me. Scan is set for early April.

documents.title: RE: Done!
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations, Jennifer - that's a big milestone. I'll watch for the scan results. Let's get you in after that for a full visit and labs.

documents.title: Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Hematology/Oncology follow-up.

DLBCL, stage I with B symptoms, left neck. Completed R-CHOP x6 on 02/26/2026.

End-of-treatment PET-CT 04/09/2026: complete metabolic response, Deauville 2. No residual FDG-avid disease.

She feels well, energy returning, no night sweats or fevers.

Plan: surveillance visits with exam and labs every 3 months for the first two years. Routine imaging not planned unless symptoms. Rheumatology to manage RA from here.
Hematology/Oncology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: First in-person visit since finishing chemo. PET in April showed complete response. Energy maybe 80%. Back at the office full time. No sweats, fevers or new lumps. Saw rheumatology 4/28: joints quiet since the chemo, staying on prednisone 5 mg alone, no new arthritis drug for now, they'll revisit if she flares. Bowels normal. Surveillance colonoscopy got pushed by chemo, now set for June.

Meds: levothyroxine 100 mcg, prednisone 5 mg, ferrous sulfate 325 mg, clobetasol twice weekly.

O: weight 64 kg. Neck without adenopathy. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no organomegaly. Hands without synovitis.

A/P
1. DLBCL in complete metabolic response - oncology surveillance q3mo.
2. Iron deficiency anemia - CBC, ferritin.
3. Hypothyroidism - TSH.
4. RA - on prednisone alone per rheum.
5. Adenoma surveillance - colonoscopy June.
Annual in September.

documents.title: Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 12.4, ferritin 58 - anemia resolved and stores recovering. TSH normal. Kidney and liver tests normal. Continue iron for now, messaged her.

reports.text:
Specimen: ascending colon, resection scar, cold forceps biopsies, three fragments.

Microscopic: colonic mucosa with preserved crypt architecture and mild submucosal fibrosis. No adenomatous change.
reports.conclusion: Benign colonic mucosa. Negative for adenoma and dysplasia.

documents.title: Colonoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Surveillance colonoscopy 06/11/2026, one year after piecemeal EMR of a 22 mm tubulovillous adenoma with high-grade dysplasia (interval extended for lymphoma treatment).

Prep adequate. Cecum reached. Clipped resection scar in the ascending colon, flat and pale, with no residual polyp; scar biopsied. Remainder of the colon normal.

Impression: no residual adenoma at the EMR site.
Recommendation: repeat colonoscopy in 1 year. Copy to PCP.

documents.title: Good news week
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Two good reports to pass on. The colonoscopy last month was clear where they took the polyp, next one in a year. And I saw oncology on the 16th for my 3-month check - exam and blood work all fine, no sign of the lymphoma. Next one in October. See you in September for my physical.

documents.title: RE: Good news week
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wonderful news, thank you for letting us know! The doctor saw your message. Your physical is on the books for September 15.
